title: cost-optimization: autotune batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: reduce per-token unit economics across common workloads by improving defaults and adding autotune plumbing. This PR centralizes batching and prefix/KV-caching defaults, adds quantization profile metadata and selection heuristics to the model registry, and wires a lightweight unit-economics (UEcon) scoring service into the Console and CLI so engineers can see expected cost/latency tradeoffs.

Summary of changes (single-string description that includes checklists and context):
- Batching/caching defaults: introduce runtime heuristics that choose per-model default target_batch_ms and cache_eviction thresholds based on historical sequence length distributions and tail latency SLOs. Adds continuous-tolerance mode to avoid regressing p95 under bursty traffic.
- Quant profiles: add quant_profiles.yaml schema to model-registry and selection logic in the runtime that prefers smaller quant profiles for cost-sensitive tiers while preserving quality thresholds. Support fallback ordering for mixed-precision variants.
- Unit-econ tooling: new uecon microservice (Console + CLI) that simulates per-route cost given model/quant/batching/caching settings and typical request distributions. Exposes a simple API and a Console dashboard component for engineers to compare options.
- Opt-in autotune controller: a controller that can emit recommended overrides for reserved pools / dedicated capacity based on observed throughput and cost. The controller is off by default; enabling requires feature flag.

Checklist:
- [x] Runtime heuristics implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Quant profile schema + model-registry migration script
- [x] UEcon API + Console dashboard component + basic e2e test
- [x] Documentation updates and example config
- [x] Perf validation: end-to-end benchmark (internal perf lab)

Performance summary (perf lab):
- Common web chat workload (avg seq 120, p95 512): median token cost reduction ~22%, P50 latency unchanged, P95 latency +3% (within SLO).
- Short prompt bursty traffic: ~18% cost reduction with continuous-tolerance mode (p95 impact <5%).

Backward compatibility & rollout: defaults are additive; autotune controller and UEcon API are gated behind feature flags. Model-registry migration adds optional quant_profiles metadata; existing models are unaffected.

Why this PR is large: touches runtime scheduler, model-registry, console, and docs to provide an end-to-end developer experience for cost-aware defaults. The goal is to make the first-pass defaults much better so engineers need fewer manual tweaks to hit cost targets.

Related: ENG-3421 (autotune staging), ENG-3499 (uecon dashboard), SUP-2148 (customer-reported runaway token costs).

reviews: Connor Lee (request changes): Please include more details on how continuous-tolerance mode behaves under extreme burstiness. Observed in perf that naive batching increases p95 >10% for some traces.

Aisha Patel (reply): Continuous-tolerance mode limits batch sizing growth when observed p95 exceeds configured latency SLO. Added an adaptive backoff and a hard cap per model (configurable). See runtime/scheduler.go comments and unit tests. Also added perf test that simulates bursty arrivals.
Marta Nguyen (comment): Quant profile schema looks good. Please add a migration note for model owners and a small CLI to preview chosen profile for a model.
Aisha Patel (reply): Added migration SQL and a cli 'redwood model show-quant' command. Documentation updated to include migration steps.
Diego Alvarez (approve): Verified perf runs in perf lab and eyeballed Console screenshots. Approving to merge once CI green and lint fixed.
release_notes: Adds smarter defaults for batching and KV-caching, quantization profile support in the model registry, and a Unit-Economics simulation tool available in Console and CLI. Feature flags control autotune controller. See docs for migration and enabling instructions.
notes_on_testing: Perf lab tests were run against ded-4g pool with three representative workloads (web-chat, code-assist, long-context summarization). Tests include a baseline run, default heuristic run, and autotune run. Results summarized above. Added unit tests for schema validation and scheduler backoff logic.
